title: Welcome to Mind
subtitle: A guided tour of your second brain
description: An interactive walkthrough of the Mind app: open it, land on the Mind Home dashboard, and meet each of the 16 memory windows — people, teams, projects, meetings, decisions, incidents, action items, wins, competencies, evidence, reviews, goals, topics, patterns, gotchas and notes — learning what each holds and how they link into one knowledge graph.

steps.title: Welcome to Mind
steps.body:
**Mind** is your second brain — persistent memory that survives across AI sessions. It holds the people, projects, decisions, wins and lessons of your work, and every record links to the others, so the **graph builds itself** as you go.

Let's open it and walk through each part. Use **Next** to step along, or **Esc** to leave anytime.

steps.title: Open your menu
steps.body: Everything starts from the **menu** on the left. Click any highlighted button to open it — I'll continue as soon as it's open.

steps.title: Open the Mind app
steps.body: Here's the **Mind** app in your menu. Click its name to open it — you'll land straight on its home dashboard.

steps.title: Mind Home
steps.body: This is **Mind Home** — the app's default dashboard, now set as your desktop background. Each tile is a live window onto one kind of memory. Let's look at them one at a time.

steps.title: People
steps.body: **People** are everyone you work with — colleagues, stakeholders, contacts. Most other records point back here, so when you remember a decision or a meeting, you also remember **who** was part of it.

steps.title: Projects
steps.body: **Projects** are the initiatives and efforts you're involved in. They're the spine of the graph — meetings, decisions, action items, wins and incidents all link to the project they belong to.

steps.title: Meetings
steps.body: **Meetings** capture who met, when, and what came out of it. Link the people who attended and the project it concerned, and the meeting becomes a searchable point in your timeline rather than a lost calendar entry.

steps.title: Wins
steps.body: **Wins** are the things that went well — shipped features, solved problems, good calls. Tie each to the competencies it demonstrates and you've got ready-made evidence for your next review.

steps.title: Decisions
steps.body: **Decisions** record the choices you made and — crucially — **why**. Six months later, when someone asks "why did we do it this way?", the reasoning is right here instead of lost to memory.

steps.title: Action Items
steps.body: **Action Items** are the follow-ups and to-dos that fall out of meetings, decisions and incidents. Each links back to where it came from, so nothing gets orphaned.

steps.title: Notes
steps.body: **Notes** are the free-form catch-all — anything that doesn't fit a tidier box yet. The rich markdown body is the content; add a person or project ref and even a loose note joins the graph.

steps.title: Goals
steps.body: **Goals** are what you're working toward — quarterly objectives, growth targets, personal aims. Progress on them is told by the wins, projects and competencies that point at them.

steps.title: Incidents
steps.body: **Incidents** are when things went wrong — outages, breakages, mistakes. Capturing the what and the fix turns a bad day into a durable lesson, and often spawns action items and gotchas.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.body: **Evidence** is the proof behind your story — links, artifacts, metrics, quotes. It backs up competencies and reviews so claims about your impact aren't just assertions.

steps.title: Competencies
steps.body: **Competencies** are the skills you're building and demonstrating. Wins and evidence link in as proof, and reviews assess them — this is where your professional growth is tracked over time.

steps.title: Reviews
steps.body: **Reviews** are your performance reviews and retrospectives. They cite the competencies assessed and the evidence behind them, so a review writes itself from the graph you've already built.

steps.title: Topics
steps.body: **Topics** are the subjects and areas of knowledge you care about. Use them to group notes, patterns and gotchas around a theme so related learnings cluster together.

steps.title: Patterns
steps.body: **Patterns** are the recurring shapes you've noticed — approaches that keep working, situations that keep repeating. Naming a pattern once lets you reuse the insight everywhere it applies.

steps.title: Gotchas
steps.body: **Gotchas** are the traps learned the hard way — the surprising footguns and edge cases. Writing one down means you (or your AI) never get caught by it twice.

steps.title: Teams
steps.body: **Teams** are the groups people belong to. Link a person to their team and a project to the teams behind it, and you can see the human structure around any piece of work.

steps.title: That's your second brain!
steps.body:
You've met all sixteen kinds of memory — **people**, **teams** and **projects**; the work itself in **meetings**, **decisions**, **action items**, **incidents** and **wins**; your growth in **competencies**, **evidence**, **reviews** and **goals**; and your knowledge in **notes**, **topics**, **patterns** and **gotchas**.

The magic is the **links between them** — fill in the refs and the graph builds itself. Just talk to your AI as you work, and Mind remembers. Check the **Help Center** anytime.
